declarations.description:
One row of an Accordion: a header holding the title and its disclosure
control, and the content it reveals. Use inside `<zds-accordion>`, which
opens and closes it and decides whether it is selectable, its divider and
its control's shape.

The disclosure control is a native `button` with `aria-expanded` /
`aria-controls` in this row's shadow root, next to the `region` panel it
controls. On a selectable row it is drawn with Icon Button's subtle /
medium tokens rather than nesting `<zds-icon-button>`: that element's
button sits in its own shadow root, where `aria-expanded` and
`aria-controls` can't reach it or the panel. The rest of a selectable row
is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`. A disabled row's disclosure button
stays focusable with `aria-disabled` (as Base UI's trigger does in React);
its selection button is natively disabled (as Base UI's Toggle is).

declarations.description:
A vertically stacked list of disclosure rows sharing one container, for a
page that has more sections than it has room to show at once. Holds
`<zds-accordion-item>` rows.

The same semantics as the React package's Base UI Accordion, built
natively: each row's header is a heading holding a `button` with
`aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`, its panel a `region` labelled by that
button; one row open at a time unless `multiple`; Up / Down / Home / End
move focus between this accordion's own headers (wrapping), Enter / Space
open and close. The panel height animates with Switch's spring, and not at
all under reduced motion.

Built apart from `<zds-collapsible-card>` (spec analysis): that is one card
that folds, this is a list of rows with one shared outline.

declarations.description:
Offers a contextual action, or stands for an item someone can discard,
such as an attached file. Five colours borrow the status tokens to mark a
state or a kind of item, and `foreground`, `background` and `border`
override any one paint beyond those five (override > color > state).
Reach for `<zds-button>` when the action is the primary next step, and
`<zds-filter-chip>` when the control narrows content.

Without `discardable` the chip is one native button; listen for `click`.
With it, a button cannot hold another, so the chip becomes a group holding
the label (a button only when `clickable` is set) and a remove control
that fires `zds-discard`, as `<zds-input-chip>` does. Not modelled from
Figma (spec issues): the single-value `active` axis and State=selected.
28px tall in every state (Figma's 30/28 jump is a layout artefact of its
inside border).

declarations.description:
A swatch that isn't one of the seven named ones: a token name
(`chart/series/2`), a custom property (`--brand-accent`) or any CSS colour.

A visual representation of a user or entity, shown as a photo, initials,
or icon, with an optional status indicator.

Nine sizes step from xxxsmall to xxxlarge with medium as the base; only
medium's width, ring weight and initials font size are bound to real
tokens (`control-lg`, `stroke-thick`, `label-large/font-size`) — every
other step is an authored value carried over from Figma as-is (spec
issue). Badge size and initials font size are otherwise unbound and are
implemented here as exactly one third of the avatar's own size, matching
the ratio measured across all nine Figma variants. The ring is drawn
outside the avatar's content circle rather than inset over it.

Content type, swatch colour, presence status and the custom status icon
are all swap-only in Figma, not exposed component properties there — this
element exposes them as real properties because a consumer has to set them
somehow (see the spec's `internalVariations`).

Theming: every colour is a semantic token, so an `.ext-*` / `.mode-*` class
on any ancestor re-themes the avatar with no re-render.

declarations.description:
Shows a group of people as overlapping avatars, with an optional counter
standing in for everyone who did not fit. Size moves the whole rail
together rather than any single avatar.

The avatars are slotted `<zds-avatar>` elements. The rail owns their
presentation, as the spec's "parent owned" row says: it sets each one's
`size` and turns off its ring, dismiss badge and presence badge, so the
group stays uniform; the person shown is the only thing set per avatar.
`max` sets how many avatars show (2 to 4, the spec's four positions with
the first two always present); Figma does the same with Show Avatar 3/4.
Avatars past `max` are given `hidden` (and given back if they come into
range), and the counter is generated from them: "+" and the avatars
passed in less `max`, a remainder rather than a total (owner decision,
2026-10-18). It shows while `show-overflow` is on and there is a
remainder, so a trimmed group never reads as complete.

Static: no hover, focus or press, and no motion (spec).

current page. `max-items` collapses the middle into a compact overflow menu,

declarations.description:
A surface anchored to the bottom edge of the screen, holding supplementary
content or a short set of actions. `content-type` lays out `zds-menu-item`
rows, `zds-grid-menu-item` tiles or anything else.

By default it only draws the surface, and the screen presents it. With
`modal`, it presents itself: a native `<dialog>` anchored to the bottom of
the viewport over a `<zds-scrim>` (tone scrim), focus moved in and returned,
page scroll locked, and Escape or a scrim click closing it when
`dismissible`. It rises from the bottom edge (animations/smooth; none under
reduced motion). Figma defines no motion, so that is a code decision.

Departures from Figma, each a spec issue:
- `heading`, `header-icon`, `show-leading-icon`, `header-alignment` and the
  `actions` slot are inputs, because Figma sets them on nested instances.
- The sheet fills its container (Figma ships a fixed 360).

declarations.description:
A pattern, not a single visual component: a trigger paired with a
`zds-dropdown-menu` positioned relative to it. `open` shows or hides the
menu, `position` picks which side it opens on, and `align` pins which pair
of edges line up (spec: "Align pins opposite edges together" — with
Position bottom/top the menu's left/right edge lines up with the
trigger's, with Position left/right its top/bottom edge does).

Composition: the spec's own anatomy nests the Dropdown Menu instance
*inside* the template, pinned to `Rounded=true` and exposed so its slot is
reachable from outside ("Menu content goes into the nested menu's slot,
not the template"). This element mirrors that rather than asking a
consumer to place a `zds-dropdown-menu` themselves: the trigger goes in the
named `trigger` slot, and everything else — `zds-menu-item` rows — goes in
the default slot, which this element forwards into its own internal
`zds-dropdown-menu`. `rounded` is exposed here (defaulting `true`, matching
the spec's pinned value) so a consumer can still opt into square corners
without reaching into the panel directly.

Positioning is pure CSS: `.panel` is `position: absolute` against `:host`
(`position: relative`, already hugging just the trigger per the spec), with
one rule per `position` value setting the matching offset (`top: 100%` for
`bottom`, cleared by `--space-sm` — 8px, matching the spec's stated fixed
gap) and one rule per applicable `position`×`align` pair pinning the
cross-axis edge — see dropdown.styles.ts. No `getBoundingClientRect`, no
resize/scroll listeners, no `position: fixed` viewport math.

An earlier version used `position: fixed` plus JS-computed `top`/`left` in
viewport coordinates, recomputed on open/resize/scroll. That broke
specifically on Storybook's Docs page: Docs wraps each embedded story in a
zoomable/scaled preview frame, and `position: fixed` resolves against
whichever ancestor introduces a `transform` (the zoom's scale), not the
viewport — so JS math done in true viewport coordinates landed the panel
somewhere that transformed frame never painted it, and the menu appeared
not to open at all there even though the same story rendered correctly in
Canvas (no transformed ancestor). Anchoring to `:host` with plain CSS
offsets has no viewport coordinate to get wrong in the first place, so the
whole bug class doesn't apply.

No collision detection: the spec itself says flipping `position` near a
viewport edge is the implementation's job ("nothing here stops it opening
off-screen... is the implementation's job"), and this is an intentional,
documented scope reduction versus the React sibling package's Base UI Menu
(which gets that for free from floating-ui) rather than an oversight.

declarations.description:
The floating panel a `zds-dropdown` opens onto — a menu surface with its
own elevation, holding a list of `zds-menu-item` rows.

The spec models this panel as two fixed built-in rows above a slot that
takes "the rest", with each `rounded` variant storing that slot's content
separately in Figma (spec issue: "Each Rounded variant stores this slot's
content separately, so switching Rounded leaves behind whatever was placed
in it"). That split is a Figma-authoring artifact — a component in code has
no reason to distinguish "the first two rows" from "the rest" — so this
element just slots everything through one default slot rather than
reproducing a built-in/more-items distinction that would only exist to
mirror how the design file happens to be organised.

The panel has no interaction states of its own (spec: "Hover, selection,
focus and disabled all live on the Menu Item rows inside it"), so this
element carries no `state` property — only `rounded`, which the panel and
its rows should agree on, and `compact`, which tightens the panel's inset.

"Should agree on" is enforced, not just documented (spec: "Rounded
propagation" behavior, added alongside Menu Item's own "match the panel"
guidance). Every slotted `zds-menu-item` that doesn't carry an explicit
`rounded` attribute of its own is kept in sync with this panel's `rounded`
— on slot assignment and whenever this panel's `rounded` changes. A row
that *does* set its own `rounded` in markup is left alone, so a consumer
can still override a single row on purpose.

declarations.description:
A glyph from the Zebra icon font.

Renders the glyph as a character rather than an SVG. `@font-face` is
registered on the document and reaches into shadow roots, but the
`.zds-icon-*` class rules from icons.css do not — so this component looks the
character up itself and only sets the family. Load `icons.css` (or at least
its `@font-face` blocks) once in the host page.

Colour comes from `currentColor` — the whole reason to ship icons as a
font: an icon inside a button inherits that button's colour with no extra
rule and no per-flavour wiring. `size` binds the glyph's own dimension
token (`control-icon-xs/sm/md/lg`); `framed` pads it to a fixed box,
40px (`control-target-min`) or 24px (`control-xs`) at xsmall, for a
standalone tappable icon. A
component that already provides its own target area, like Button, locks
both rather than leaving them open to the consumer.

Both families share codepoints, so `sharp` is a family swap, never a
content change. The spec pins this axis to rounded and does not expose it
(spec issue 1); this component exposes it deliberately since both families
ship in the font at no extra cost.

A status message placed inside the content it is about (a form, a card, a
panel), not pinned to the screen like `<zds-system-banner>`. It sits in the
flow at the width of its container.

Five statuses, each in two appearances. solid: the strong feedback fill with
foreground/on-strong text, for the one message on a view that must be seen
now. subtle: the faint feedback tint with a status border and the status
colour on the glyph only, for context and guidance.

On solid, Figma pins palette=Dark on the action slot and the dismiss so they
draw light on any fill. Slotted actions live in the light DOM, so the banner
puts `.mode-dark` on them. The dismiss lives in the shadow root, where the
document's mode classes can't reach, so on solid it maps its foreground to
foreground/on-strong instead; its hover scrim follows the page mode.

gap: no size token). The description and the actions render when they are
set, which is the spec's showDescription and showActions. The title is
`heading` (a `title` attribute would also show the browser's tooltip).

declarations.description:
The text entry control on its own, without a label or hint around it. One
model covers five input types, Text, Number, Password, Date and Time, which
share the same Size, Shape, State and Flavour and differ only in their
placeholder and in the control sitting at the trailing edge. Reach for it
directly when a field needs no label or supporting text, and reach for
`<zds-input>` when it does.

Figma builds one component set per type; here they are one element with a
`type`. On a native `<input>`:
- **text**: optional `trailing-icon` (the spec's hasTrailing, off by default).
- **number**: native numeric input; arrow keys step it. Its trailing icon
  defaults to `dialpad` (the spec's hasTrailing, on by default); set
  `trailing-icon=""` for none.
- **password**: a reveal control, always present.
- **date**, **time**: a `calendar-3-day` / `clock-outline` control opening
  the platform picker, always present. No leading icon.

State, as the spec's run enabled → focus → selected → typing → filled:
keyboard focus on an empty field is `focus`, pointer focus `selected`, any
focus with a value `typing` (the only state offering clear), a value at
rest `filled`. `invalid`, `readonly` and `disabled` are set by the form.
`:focus-visible` cannot separate keyboard from pointer focus on a text
input, so the modality is tracked from pointerdown.

A full-size preview over the page: images, videos and PDFs render
themselves; anything else shows a drawn file sheet with its glyph and
"no preview". A toolbar names the item and offers open in a new tab,
download and close; previous / next page through the items (buttons and
arrow keys). Each control hides behind its `show-*` attribute.

Paging slides a track of frames rather than swapping one for another: the
neighbouring items stay mounted either side of the current one, so moving
between them never reloads media or flickers, and the old frame glides out
as the new one glides in on one CSS transition (`animated`, yielding to
reduced motion). The stage's height follows the current frame on the same
timing, measured again when media reports real dimensions — sizes arrive
after mount, so the first measure is never final. Opening is different: the
panel springs in from the bottom (animations/spring) with the stage already
at the first frame's height — the height never animates on open.

Modal behaviour — the top layer, the inert page, Escape, scroll lock and
focus return — comes from the native `<dialog>` and `showModal()`, exactly
as `zds-dialog`. Kept in step with packages/react-baseui `<Lightbox>`.

A single selectable row inside a `zds-dropdown-menu` (or any menu-shaped
list built without one).

`type` picks what leads the row. Icon rows take `leading-icon`; checkbox
and radio rows lead with a real `zds-checkbox` / `zds-radio` at size
medium, checked when the row is `selected` and disabled with it. Figma
leaves that control unchecked in every state (spec warn), so code follows
the row instead. The control only shows state: the row stays the one
interactive element, with the matching ARIA role (`menuitemcheckbox` /
`menuitemradio`), and the control is inert and hidden from assistive
technology. The whole row is the click target: activating a checkbox row
toggles `selected`, a radio row selects itself and clears the radio rows
beside it, and both fire `change`.

`state` in the spec is mostly CSS: hover and focus are real `:hover` /
`:focus-visible`. `selected` is the one state Figma models that has no
native pseudo-class, so it is the one exposed as a property here (folding
in "selected focus" too, since that is just selected + real :focus-visible
together).

The spec's `leadingElement` boolean and the implicit "which Icon instance"
choice are collapsed into one `leading-icon` property, the same way
`zds-button` already turns "is there a leading icon" + "which one" into a
single nullable prop rather than a separate visibility toggle.

The app's destinations in a tall panel at the edge of the screen, opened
from a menu button.

Built from the Navigation Rail family, with no new parts: a
`zds-navigation-header` in the `header` slot, then `zds-sub-menu-item`

`<zds-scrim>` (tone scrim). Focus moves in and returns, page scroll is
locked, and Escape, a scrim click, the header's close button or a chosen
destination closes it. It slides in from its edge (animations/smooth;
none under reduced motion).

nothing and is inert.

Scrolling: only the header is frozen (sticky). The menu never scrolls on
its own and the footer is never pinned. The standard drawer grows with its
content and the page scrolls it; the modal drawer scrolls as one surface
with no scrollbar.

With `show-close` (default) the header's icon button is the close button:
the drawer sets its glyph to `close` and its label to `close-label`.

declarations.description:
A vertical navigation column for the edge of a desktop view: a narrow icon
rail or a wide labelled one, and an optional sub menu panel beside it.

Follows the page's mode by default. `inverse` shows the opposite shade,
and `locked` keeps the rail dark (light with `inverse`) whatever the page
does. For either, the host takes the token layer's `mode-*` class (added
with `classList`, so a consumer's own classes stay), which re-resolves
every token on the host; the shadow tree and the slotted content inherit
them from there, and an `.ext-*` ancestor still applies. Nothing in the
rail family leaves the tree, so popups stay in mode.

Regions are slots; the rail sets `expanded` / `show-label` on the
zds-navigation-rail-item and zds-navigation-header elements inside it, and
`shape` on every rail part inside it (items, headers, sub menu rows and
groups). Slotted controls it did not render — a zds-sub-menu-header's
actions — read `el.closest("zds-navigation-rail")?.shape` to match, as
with zds-table. It
owns the toggle item and wires it to `expanded` (spec: "Behaviour code
must own"), firing `zds-expanded-change`.

A plain `<nav>` of links, every destination in the Tab order; groups are
zds-collapsible-menu-item disclosures — the same structure as the React
build (which uses Base UI Collapsible, not NavigationMenu).

Figma's Show Header (wired to nothing) is dropped — the header shows when
slotted. Its per-Label Menu Slots and orphan Menu Slot#3200:20 are one
default slot; moreRailItems / moreFooterItems / showHeaderAction /
showSubMenu become "is the slot filled".

declarations.description:
Which page numbers to show. The spec leaves this to code ("Paging
behaviour isn't modelled"); this is the shared contract the React package
implements too, so keep the two identical.

visible = min(visiblePages, pageCount); the window is centred on the
current page and clamped to the range. With showMore the last page always
appears — in the window, as the next number, or after "…". The overflow's
`page` is the first hidden page, where activating it goes.

A horizontal bar of page controls: first/previous/next/last jump buttons,
a window of page number indicators, and an overflow marker with the last
page for a long range. Used inside Table Footer and anywhere else a result
set is split across pages.

Renders nothing while `pageCount` is 1 or less: the spec says a single-page
bar shouldn't exist, so the element simply takes no space.

Controlled like Table's sort: activating a control sets `page` and fires
`zds-page-change`, so it works with no listener; a listener that owns the
page can still overwrite it. The current page carries
`aria-current="page"`; jumps at the ends are natively `disabled`.

`outline` and `rounded` are whole-bar styling (spec: no per-button
override). Glyphs are pinned to the rounded family, as Figma draws them.

Theming: every colour is a semantic token, so an `.ext-*` / `.mode-*`
class on any ancestor re-themes the bar with no re-render.

sets the flag and dial code, the field groups digits as they are typed, and

A horizontal track that fills to show how far an ongoing process has got,
with an indeterminate mode and a buffered band for when the extent is not
known, and an optional label row above it.

`value` is a real number between `min` and `max` (Figma's 0/25/50/100%
variants are samples of it); `value = null` (or removing the attribute) is
indeterminate, a short segment sliding along the track. `buffering` turns
on Figma's Buffering band (determinate only), from the start of the track up to `buffer` (how
much has preloaded); `value` never runs past it.

Accessibility mirrors Base UI's Progress (the React package): the bar is a
`role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin/max/now` and an `aria-valuetext`
of the formatted percentage, or "indeterminate progress" plus `aria-busy`
with no `aria-valuenow`. It is named by the label row, or by `label` when
the row is hidden. The progressbar is the bar only, so a control slotted
into `trailing` stays reachable.

Theming: every colour is a semantic token, so an `.ext-*` / `.mode-*` class
on any ancestor re-themes it. Kept in step with React `<ProgressBar>`.

optional file-transfer control (percentage readout, or cancel) at its

named by `cancel-label`. The readout is aria-hidden: it repeats the value.

inside those rings (Figma leaves it out there too).

declarations.description:
A single-line input for typing a query, with a magnifier leading it and a
trailing control that takes whatever icon and function the implementation
passes.

Built on a native `<input type="search">`, so the caret, selection, text
editing and form submission are the browser's. The spec's State axis is
not a property; it follows from the field:
- **hover**: pointer over the field.
- **focus**: keyboard focus on an empty field — the heaviest border.
- **selected**: focus by pointer, before any text — a lighter border.
- **typing**: focused with text in it. The clear control appears.
- **filled**: text in it, not focused.
- **disabled**: the `disabled` property.

The clear control and the trailing control are real buttons, each with a
pressable area wider than its glyph (spec warn "the control targets aren't
modelled"). The trailing control does nothing by itself: listen for
`trailing-click` and give it a name with `trailing-label`.

The field has no label of its own (spec accessibility): set `label`, or
point an `aria-labelledby` at a visible one.

Not built: the spec's `Show Cancel` property, which Figma wires to nothing
(spec warn "Show Cancel is wired to nothing").

declarations.description:
A control for choosing a value along a range by dragging a thumb.

Behaviour comes from native `<input type="range">` elements in the shadow
root — one, or two in range mode. They provide the `slider` role with its
value, minimum and maximum (spec accessibility: "exposed as a number
together with its minimum and maximum"), arrow / Page / Home / End keys, and
pointer dragging. The track, active fill and step dots are drawn behind
them; the inputs' own thumbs are restyled.

Mapping from the spec:
- `state` is not a property. `disabled` is `disabled`. The larger thumb
  size follows the pointer only: the thumb under it, or being dragged, grows,
  and the other doesn't, in every state. `selected` is colour only: the fill
  and both thumbs take the selected foreground during a drag or while a
  thumb has keyboard focus, and the focused thumb also gets a focus ring
  (spec "designerClarifications").
- `value`, `min`, `max`, `step` and `valueStart` have no Figma reference
  (spec blocker "nothing models the value, minimum, maximum or step");
  they follow the native range input.
- `stepped` draws one dot per stop, derived from min, max and step,
  rather than from slotted dots — so the dots sit at the values they mark,
  across the whole track (spec warn "the step dots span the full track
  only at 50%").
- `range` adds a start thumb, and the fill runs between the two thumbs:
  a true span, which the Figma structure can't draw (spec warn "range mode
  can't show a span that doesn't start at the minimum").

In range mode each thumb needs its own name (spec accessibility); set
`label` and `start-label`.

Theming: every colour is a semantic token, so an `.ext-*` / `.mode-*` class
on any ancestor re-themes the slider with no JavaScript.

declarations.description:
A brief message about something the app just did, carrying at most one
action. Variant chooses between a contextual pill, where Status sets the
tint, the leading glyph and the controls together, and a plain standard
bar.

Follows specs/snackbar:
 - contextual info / positive / warning / negative / deletion / view sit on
   feedback/<kind>/background/subtle (negative and deletion take error, view takes
   neutral) with their glyph; action, default and every standard bar are
   the dark bars, on surface/overlay.
 - The action is a `<zds-button>`, subtle on deletion (Undo), view (View)
   and standard (Action), outline-subtle on action; the close a subtle
   `<zds-icon-button>`. Both are medium, full on the contextual pill,
   rounded on standard and sharp when the bar is sharp. (Figma draws the
   rounded action bar's button small; the spec warns, and medium keeps it
   concentric with the bar's end like every other control.)
 - The message stays on one line (spec: Width). Where the space runs out
   it ends in an ellipsis rather than running past the edge.

The message is the default slot. `action-label` overrides the status's
action ("" removes it); `show-close` the close. The statuses without a
glyph of their own (default, action, and every standard bar) take one in
the `icon` slot (Figma's Icon Slot / Show Icon); it is coloured and sized
(control/icon-md) like the built-in glyphs.

Behaviour: `open` shows it. With `duration` (ms) it closes itself, but the
timer pauses while the pointer or focus is inside, so nobody loses a
message they are reading or an Undo they are reaching for. Announced
politely (role=status); negative interrupts (role=alert).

Dark bars carry their own colour mode: Figma pins palette=Dark on them; in
code the host takes .mode-dark on a light page and .mode-light on a dark
one (the inversion the spec notes Figma cannot express), so every token
inside, the buttons' included, resolves in that mode. The page's mode is
read from the nearest .mode-* ancestor when the bar connects and each time
it opens.

Placement and motion (spec: Motion, Layering): it floats in the top layer
(a manual popover), so no z-index on the page can sit above it, centred
space/xl above the bottom of the viewport. It slides in from below over
300ms and leaves sliding up and fading over 200ms (no motion tokens yet);
with reduced motion it only fades. `inline` keeps it in the page flow
instead, for documentation.

declarations.description:
A numeric value with a button on either side to decrease or increase it,
and an optional hint below.

The number model matches the React package's Base UI NumberField: a typed
value is kept (clamped to `min` / `max` on blur or Enter), the buttons
disable at the bounds, pressing and holding a button repeats, ArrowUp /
ArrowDown step (Shift for `large-step`), PageUp / PageDown move by
`large-step`, Home / End jump to `min` / `max`. The input is a
`role="spinbutton"` with aria-valuenow / -min / -max; the buttons are out of
the tab order (the keyboard drives the input) but stay pressable by pointer
and assistive technology.

(outline-subtle, `remove` / `add`), the value box is `<zds-input-field>`'s
own stylesheet, the hint is Input Hint, so each keeps its own hover, focus,
disabled and invalid states. The value box is the field's styles rather
than the element because spinbutton semantics must sit on the native input,
which the element's shadow root would hide.

declarations.description:
A full-width message pinned to the top of a screen or view, carrying a
status colour, a title, an optional description and an optional action.
It spans its container and stays until something clears it.

Locked to Dark (spec: modeLock): Figma pins palette=Dark on every variant,
so the host always carries .mode-dark in the light DOM and every token
inside, the dismiss `<zds-icon-button>` and the slotted actions included,
resolves dark whatever mode the page is in. That is what keeps the
foreground/primary text and the outline-contrast action white on the
strong feedback colours.

Mobile and Desktop are two Figma sets with different APIs (spec issue
"api (sibling sets)"); here they are one element with `layout`. Desktop's
Content Type is the presence of `description`, Mobile's Show Description
likewise. The title is `heading` (a `title` attribute would also show the
browser's tooltip). The dismiss is a subtle sharp `<zds-icon-button>`,
medium on mobile and small on desktop, and never shows on negative.

One shape (spec: shapeInheritance): `shape` comes from the container and
reaches the dismiss
and every slotted `<zds-button>` / `<zds-icon-button>`; no control keeps its own.

It reveals by sliding in from the top and pushing the content below down,
and removal plays that in reverse (spec: Motion): the dismiss, or `open`
set to false. `open` true again replays the reveal. Hidden means the
`hidden` attribute, set once the reverse has played.

Announced politely (role=status), negative interrupts (role=alert).

Kept in step with packages/react-baseui `SystemBanner`.

A single on or off toggle, a track with a thumb slider that switches
between its two ends.

The host element *is* the control: it carries `role="switch"` and
`aria-checked` through ElementInternals and is form-associated, so a native

the keyboard.

- `Switch` on/off → `checked`. A two-value enum is a boolean in code (spec
  note on `api`).

  keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`), never from an attribute.

  Figma (spec `internalVariations`); here they are `onIcon` (the start
  slot, uncovered while checked) and `offIcon` (the end slot, uncovered
  while unchecked). Leave both unset for a plain track and thumb.

on any ancestor re-themes the switch with no JavaScript.

A short floating message that names what an adjacent control does.

Point it at its trigger with `for` (an id in the same document or shadow
root) or the `anchor` property. It then lives in the top layer as a manual
popover — clear of any `overflow: hidden` ancestor, still inside the theme
cascade because it stays in this element's shadow tree — and:

- opens after `delay` ms of hover, at once on keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`);
- stays open while the pointer moves onto the bubble;
- closes on pointer leave (after `close-delay`), blur, a press on the
  trigger, or Escape;
- is placed on the side opposite `point`, flips when that side would leave
  the viewport, shifts along the edge to stay on screen, and aims the

  `zds-icon-button` — as that element's `ariaDescribedByElements`). The
  trigger still needs its own accessible name.

With no trigger it renders the static bubble in flow — the component
exactly as the spec draws it.

positioning: `anchor-name` cannot reach from a light-DOM trigger into this
shadow root, and Firefox/Safari support is too recent for the package's
targets.

declarations.description:
A data table with rows of content in columns, framed by an optional
controls bar above and a footer below.

A real `<table>` (header cells `scope="col"`, `aria-sort` on sortable
columns) inside a scrolling wrapper. Figma builds the table column by
column; that is a Figma-only arrangement, the markup is row-major. Width
follows the container, not the spec's 979px sample.

Data comes in as two JS properties, `columns` and `rows`. A cell value is
text, or `{ title, subtitle?, avatar? }` for the spec's avatar-and-text
cell. Any cell can be replaced with markup through a named slot,
`cell-<rowKey>-<colKey>`, whose fallback is the data.

**Sorting, search, filters, paging.** A sortable header cycles none →
ascending → descending, sets `sort` and fires `zds-sort-change`. By default
the table is controlled and the listener reorders, filters and pages
`rows`. `client-side` makes the table do it from the full `rows`: it sorts
(text, numbers by value, or the column's `compare`), keeps rows whose text
matches `searchValue` and whose cells are among the chosen `filters`, and
shows `pageSize` rows of `page`, working out the page count and the footer
summary. Sorting, searching or filtering returns to page 1. A filterable
header then opens a compact checkbox menu of the column's values (spec:
`_Table Menu` filter) and fires `zds-filter-change`; a filtered column keeps
its glyph in foreground/cursor (`_Label` Filtered). With nothing left, one
row spanning every column reads `emptyLabel` (`_Empty Row`).

**Selection** (`selectable`, spec `_Select Cell`). A checkbox column leads
the columns, with select-all in its header, indeterminate while only some
rows shown are selected. `selectedRows` holds the keys (seeded from each
row's `selected` until set); every toggle fires `zds-selection-change`.
Select-all covers the actionable rows shown, so a selection on another
page survives. Selected rows take the selected fill across every column.
While rows are selected, an info Badge Label at the start of the controls
bar counts them (`selectedCountFormat`), in a live region.

**Row actions** (`rowActions`, spec `_Actions Cell`). A trailing small
subtle more button per row opens a compact menu of the row's actions; a
row's own `actions` replace them and `null` hides the button. Choosing one
closes the menu, calls `onRowAction` and fires `zds-row-action`.

**Menus** open as manual popovers in the top layer, clear of the table's
clipping, holding a compact `zds-dropdown-menu`. Arrow keys, Home and End
move, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger, Tab or a press
outside closes.

**Column settings** (`columnConfigure`). A settings button at the end of
the controls bar opens a panel: Show columns checkboxes (`hiddenColumns`;
the last column showing and `hideable: false` columns stay) and Freeze up
to radios (`frozenColumns`), firing `zds-column-settings-change`. Hidden
columns leave the whole table, search included.

**Resizing** (`resizable`, spec `_Header Cell` Resize). Each header's
trailing edge is a focusable separator; hovering shows
interactive/neutral/border/hover at full cell height. A resize never
changes the table's width: a column grows by taking width from the
resizable columns after it (nearest first, none below `minColumnWidth`) and
shrinks by giving it to the next; the last column trades with those before
it. Drag, arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps), Home for the minimum, and a
double-click or Escape resets. Each change fires `zds-column-resize`. The
first resize locks every column at its rendered width and switches to fixed
layout, so widths land exactly and narrow text ends in an ellipsis.

**Truncation.** Cut-off text shows in full in a `zds-tooltip` after
`tooltipDelay` ms of hover; a column's `tooltip` shows it even when the text
fits, `tooltipOnEllipsisOnly: false` turns it off. It repeats text already
on the page, so it is not wired up as a description.

**Disabled rows.** A row is disabled by its own `disabled` or by its key
in `disabledRows`: every cell keeps the plain fill, text turns
foreground/disabled and avatars and slotted content dim (raw 0.5 opacity,
spec gap). It can't be selected, clicked or opened for actions, unless
`allowDisabledSelection`, which keeps the look but allows all three.

**Sticky header.** `maxHeight` caps the content so rows scroll under a
header that sticks to the top; frozen columns stay frozen both ways.

`frozenColumns` pins the first N columns (Table Content
`columnPosition=frozen`); their sticky offsets are measured from the
rendered header cells, the selection column freezing with them. Once the
rest scroll beneath them, the last frozen column casts a horizontal shadow.

The footer holds the page summary, an optional rows-per-page `zds-select`
(`pageSizeOptions`, compact, firing `zds-page-size-change`) and an outline
`zds-pagination` whose `zds-page-change` bubbles out of the table; anything
slotted into `pagination` replaces it.

Rows get a pointer cursor while something listens for `zds-row-click` on
the element itself (a WC has no handler prop to detect).

Theming: every colour is a semantic token, so an `.ext-*` / `.mode-*`
class on any ancestor re-themes the table with no re-render.

declarations.description:
The header at the top of a mobile screen. `type` switches between six
arrangements, each with its own leading control and content.

Departures from Figma, each a spec issue:
- `count`, `avatar-src`, `avatar-initials`, `search-value` and the leading
  label are inputs, because Figma draws them as fixed sample content.
- The title and count use foreground/primary, because Figma's raw black
  would not follow dark mode.
- contextual keeps space/md after the leading control, as the metadata says.
  Figma binds none there.
- The search field opens empty, not in Figma's typing state.
- The bar fills its container (Figma ships a fixed 390).
declarations.name: ZdsTopAppBar
